title: Establish centralized release catalog and audience slate for rolling changelogs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Release notes at Redwood are fragmented across PR descriptions, Confluence drafts, and ad-hoc email summaries. This causes duplicated work, missed stakeholder signoffs, and inconsistent customer-facing language.

Goal: Build a single canonical release catalog that maps each ship item to: audience segments, primary/secondary owners, channel(s) for announcement (customer changelog, admin console, release email, partner portal), templated customer-facing blurb, risk/rollback notes, SLOs affected, and targeted rollout window. The catalog will be the source-of-truth for internal signoff and for generating the tiered customer changelogs.

Deliverables:
- Release catalog template (CSV + Confluence page + lightweight YAML export for automation)
- Audience slate taxonomy (what constitutes "Developer", "Platform Admin", "Enterprise Security", etc.)
- Customer blurb templates (3 tiers: brief, full, technical appendix) and voice guardrails
- Signoff flow and checklist (who signs for security, docs, legal, eng)
- Lightweight automation script spec to ingest catalog rows and generate draft changelog entries + PR comment for release engineer

Links and references:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/ReleaseCatalog
- Example GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
- Existing changelog templates: drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cTEMPLATE
